# Betfair REST fixtures

**Synthetic, with the shape pinned to real captures** (#304). Generated by
`tools/samples/make_synthetic_rest_sample.py`; do not hand-edit, regenerate.

The ids, names, prices and times are invented. The league names are real,
because the mapper resolves competitions by name. What is not invented is the
shape of each node. `rest-shape.json` holds each endpoint's key paths, JSON
types, key sets and enumerated values. `RestShapeManifestIT` (the `-Preplay`
tier) reads it off real responses, and `SyntheticRestShapeTest` fails the build
if a file here uses any key, key set or status the real response for the same
endpoint did not.

The real responses are Betfair's data and are not committed. They were
captured from the live API, the first three on **2026-09-02 at 03:52Z** and
`list-market-book-after-kickoff.json` on **2026-09-04 at 04:42Z**, by
`scripts/capture-betfair-rest.py`, and hand-trimmed with every node kept
verbatim. They live in custody, at
`$RAPTOR_DATA_ROOT/betfair-rest/captured/`, beside this file's pre-#304
version.

The pin exists because the alternative has been tried. PRD #95 shipped three
sport mappers with green unit tests against hand-authored fixtures that
invented a node type Betfair never returns. All three were broken on first
contact with the real API, because the fixtures and the mappers came from the
same head and agreed only with each other.

| File | Nodes | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `list-market-catalogue.json` | 6 | One event's whole four-market bundle plus two markets from a second event, enough to exercise event grouping and every captured market type |
| `list-market-book.json` | 5 | The state half: `status` and `inplay`. **Five, not six**, as in the capture: the real book covered the first twenty ids of the catalogue query and one catalogue market fell outside it, so one catalogue market has no book row |
| `list-market-book-after-kickoff.json` | 2 | Two of the *previous night's* markets, asked for by id a full day after kickoff. `inplay: true`, `status: CLOSED`: the state discovery can no longer reach, and what `follow()` is tested against |
| `list-competitions.json` | 7 | Several competitions, including one the programme asks for by name, and not "Italian Serie B", which it also asks for. So both a name that resolves and one that does not are covered |

## What the capture settled

- **`marketType` requires `MARKET_DESCRIPTION`.** Without that projection the
  response carries `marketName` ("Over/Under 2.5 Goals") and **no**
  `marketType` at all. Re-deriving `OVER_UNDER_25` from a display label is
  precisely the menu-label-versus-canonical-code mistake PRD #115 made with
  Horse Racing country, so the query asks for the description and the mapper
  reads `description.marketType`.
- **`countryCode` is on the event**, present on all 56 markets captured, and is
  ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. `listCompetitions` separately carries
  `competitionRegion` (`"CZE"`) — a different vocabulary, and not the one to
  model country on.
- **State is not in the catalogue.** `inplay` and `status` come from
  `listMarketBook`, which is why scope makes two calls rather than one.
- **`listMarketBook` has no start-time window, and `listMarketCatalogue`
  cannot be given one wide enough.** Discovery filters `marketStartTime` to
  `[now, now + horizon]`, so a market leaves it at kickoff; the second capture
  asked for four of the previous night's ids and got all four back. This is
  what #127 turned on, and it is also why widening the window was rejected —
  a `CLOSED` market has no start time inside any window.
- **Betfair does not clear `inplay` when a market closes.** Every node in
  `list-market-book-after-kickoff.json` is `inplay: true` *and*
  `status: CLOSED`. A mapper that tested in-play before status would promote a
  finished market to LIVE and never see it end; `MarketScopeService.apply`
  checks the terminal statuses first for exactly this reason.

## Known gap

Half of the original gap is closed. `list-market-book-after-kickoff.json`
supplies a real `inplay: true` and a real `status: CLOSED`, so the mapper is
no longer asserted only against markets that had not started.

**What is still missing is a book node taken while a match is actually being
played** — `status: OPEN` with `inplay: true` — and a real `SUSPENDED` one.
Both captures so far ran in the early morning UK time. Nothing here should be
invented to fill that, and the shape pin now enforces it: `SUSPENDED` is not
in the manifest, so a synthetic book node carrying it fails the build. The
state machine's transitions are tested through the domain type in
`MarketScopeIntegrationTest`. Capture during an evening fixture into custody,
re-run `RestShapeManifestIT`, and extend the generator and the mapper tests
then.
